text:
Taylor: hey all :wave: Taylor here, first day. M2 Macbook, switched to fish. trying to run dotfiles/bootstrap and asdf to install python/node/rust. python build fails during configure with openssl errors. ssh-agent doesn't persist keys after restart. 1Password CLI prompts for SSO but I don’t have vault access yet. who do I ping for Okta/vpn/git access? any quick fish + asdf tips?

Renee: welcome Taylor! for Apple Silicon the usual pattern is to use Homebrew’s openssl and point CONFIGURE_OPTS at it. in fish I put this in ~/.config/fish/conf.d/asdf_env.fish:
```
# brew libs for building python/ruby
set -x BREW_OPENSSL (brew --prefix openssl@1.1)
set -x LDFLAGS "-L$BREW_OPENSSL/lib"
set -x CPPFLAGS "-I$BREW_OPENSSL/include"
set -x PKG_CONFIG_PATH "$BREW_OPENSSL/lib/pkgconfig"
# then when installing python via asdf
env CONFIGURE_OPTS="--with-openssl=$BREW_OPENSSL" asdf install python 3.11.6
```
That avoids relying on xcode/system openssl. if you already installed, try `asdf uninstall python 3.11.x` then reinstall after the env vars are live.

DevTools: Node plugin needs the release-team key import once: run this in a bash shell (or call from fish):
```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs/master/bin/import-release-team-keyring | bash
asdf plugin add nodejs https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf-nodejs.git
asdf install nodejs 18.16.0
```
Also FYI we keep a dotfiles bootstrap flag to skip symlinking if you want to audit changes: `./bootstrap.sh --dry-run`

Renee: for ssh on mac, prefer the macOS keychain so keys survive restarts. one-liner to add key to keychain: `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` then in fish add a tiny conf.d script to start the agent if missing:
```
# ~/.config/fish/conf.d/ssh-agent.fish
if not set -q SSH_AUTH_SOCK
  eval (ssh-agent -c) >/dev/null
  ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 >/dev/null 2>&1; or true
end
```
That fixed persisting for me.

CloudInfra: Taylor 305 - welcome! for Okta/VPN/Git access open an IT ticket: https://itsupport.redwood.internal/new and include your manager's email + employee id. If you drop the ticket number here I can expedite adding you to GitHub teams and the Okta group. ETA ~1 business day for basic access.

dev_onboard_bot: checklist created for Taylor: [create-ssh-key, add-to-1password, clone-dotfiles, install-asdf-runtimes, open-it-ticket] (0/5).

Taylor: thanks, followed Renee’s brew + CONFIGURE_OPTS suggestion and python compiled 389. ran the node key import and node installed. ssh key persisted after adding to keychain and reboot 60a. waiting on Okta invite/ticket.

Renee: glad it worked. small note: if you use VS Code Remote - Containers with fish, set the container's user shell to /opt/homebrew/bin/fish in devcontainer.json so terminals pick up asdf.

Taylor: one more: should I default to devcontainers or run services locally?

CloudInfra: use devcontainers where provided (consistent dev env + fewer host-specific gotchas). for lower-level things (native rust builds, experimenting with GPU stuff) you can run locally. ping the owner if the devcontainer has missing tools.

Taylor: perfect, thanks everyone! tagging here if Okta takes longer. :heart:
